run.title: Run assurance
run.detail: Generate live, governed evidence from an invoice.

inspect.title: Inspect the run
inspect.detail: Correlate the result with sanitized operational traces.

measure.title: Measure quality
measure.detail: Evaluate the current agent and verify its quality assets.

improve.title: Improve the agent
improve.detail: Search and prepare candidates without applying them.

release.title: Release with approval
release.detail: Keep live training behind review, spend, and command gates.

errors.title: Quality evidence unavailable
errors.hint: Verify that the versioned public evidence manifest is included in this deployment.

hero.title: Quality & optimization
hero.description: Follow one controlled loop: generate invoice evidence, inspect its trace, measure the agent, improve it, and require approval before release. GitHub Actions and Foundry own the work; this browser only explains the path and links to it.

governance.title: Why these operations are guarded
governance.description: Every cloud action runs in GitHub Actions so inputs, credentials, evidence, and approvals stay auditable. This page never runs cloud commands in your browser.

operations.title: From invoice evidence to a safe release
operations.detail: A controlled quality loop. Use the steps in order for a new quality cycle, or open the operation you need for an existing run.

current.label: Current
current.description: Verified by the named source within its freshness window.

referenceOnly.label: Reference only
referenceOnly.description: Commit-safe lineage for review, not a live control-plane response.

stale.label: Stale
stale.description: Past its freshness window or awaiting a new live verification.

safety.title: Safety boundary
safety.description: The workflow can run, inspect, measure, and prepare. It never auto-applies an optimizer candidate, promotes a model, or deploys an agent.
safety.gateDetail: Required reviewers and explicit spend acknowledgement are prerequisites. Submission remains blocked until a committed first-class command exists.

optimizerReview.eyebrow: Part 1 · Foundry Agent Optimizer: new assets, same model
optimizerReview.title: The optimizer improves the agent by changing its assets. The model stays {{model}}.
optimizerReview.intro: Foundry Agent Optimizer started from {{agent}} v{{version}}, used {{optimizationModel}} to write candidate prompts and tool descriptions, and scored every candidate on {{evalModel}} with the same rubric. {{candidate}} won by score.

strip.help: Score is the average evaluator score for grounding, citations, evidence shape, gap handling, and read-only behavior. This job reports scores and eval run IDs, not pass thresholds.

output.label: Output
output.text: Moved from a loose reviewer note to one strict evidence JSON object. Approval, hold, and dispute language are fenced off.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.text: Contract and policy claims now have to come from FoundryIQ context, especially {{field}}.

gaps.label: Gaps
gaps.text: Missing source documents, rate gaps, release status, and identifier-only references become controller checks.

boundary.label: Boundary
boundary.text: {{decision}} and {{action}} stay null when the request says not to decide. No system action is claimed.

prompt.label: Main prompt
prompt.text: Changed from loose triage guidance to a strict evidence JSON contract.

unchanged.label: No change
unchanged.text: Model, agent version, skills, and tool name stayed the same.

leaderboard.title: Candidate search
leaderboard.detail: {{candidates}} candidates scored · winner chosen by score

prompt.title: Main prompt changes
prompt.detail: The primary behavior contract for invoice evidence review.

emphasis.caption: Prompt emphasis
emphasis.detail: How often each behavior's key terms appear in the prompt.

shape.label: Invoice evidence shape
shape.meaning: Contract Policy Expert is told to return the exact evidence packet shape for invoice review.
shape.business: Finance reviewers and downstream checks can compare invoice findings without parsing free-form prose.

citations.label: Cited contract evidence
citations.meaning: The answer attaches source references, confidence, and support or contradiction metadata to each contract or policy claim.
citations.business: Auditors can see why an invoice line is supported, unsupported, or risky.

gaps.label: Missing-evidence handling
gaps.meaning: The agent calls out missing clauses, conflicting policy, or evidence gaps instead of inventing an answer.
gaps.business: Reduces false confidence when contract or policy evidence is incomplete.

retrieval.label: Contract and policy retrieval
retrieval.meaning: The agent searches the knowledge base for contract terms, policy rules, rate cards, SKUs, lots, and supplier evidence before deciding.
retrieval.business: Findings are grounded in Caldova's FoundryIQ source data, not generic model memory.

boundary.label: Read-only finance boundary
boundary.meaning: Contract Policy Expert explains evidence only. It must not approve invoices, reconcile payments, trigger recovery, or write back to finance systems.
boundary.business: Keeps the agent in an advisory review lane while people or controlled systems make operational decisions.

diff.legend: Line numbers: baseline, then {{candidate}}. + added, − removed.

tool.title: Retrieval tool changes
tool.detail: The tool name stayed the same. {{candidate}} tightened how the tool is described and made the search query required.
tool.behaviorChanged: Retrieval guidance is stricter about source-grounded evidence and no business-system actions.

rftPayoff.eyebrow: Part 2 · RFT: same improved assets, fine-tuned model
rftPayoff.title: RFT moves the optimized agent from gpt-6-astra to MAI.
rftPayoff.intro: These are full Foundry hosted-agent evals for {{agent}}, not model-only completions. Each stage uses {{runs}} sequential runs of {{rows}} rows against the same held-out dataset and rubric.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.detail: Intentionally weak starting assets. Results swing from run to run.

optimized.label: Optimized
optimized.detail: {{candidate}} instructions and retrieval-tool contract on gpt-6-astra.

tuned.label: Tuned MAI
tuned.detail: The same optimized assets. Only the model deployment changes.

swap.tunedDetail: The same optimized assets, swapping only to the MAI fine-tuned model deployment.

cost.title: Estimated cost: Astra vs tuned MAI
cost.pricesNote: Defaults use published Azure Global Standard rates. Edit them if this deployment uses a different meter, discount, or capacity model.
cost.savings: At {{requests}} requests, tuned MAI costs {{amount}} less than Astra ({{percent}} lower) under these price assumptions.
cost.higher: At {{requests}} requests, tuned MAI costs {{amount}} more than Astra under these price assumptions.
cost.noPrices: Enter input and output prices per 1M tokens to calculate cost. Tuned MAI emits {{tokens}} more output tokens than Astra ({{percent}}).
cost.basis: Estimated with published Azure Global Standard token rates: GPT-6 Astra at $10 input / $50 output per 1M tokens and Microsoft Code 1.1 Flash at $0.20 input / $1.20 output per 1M tokens. Foundry hosted-agent eval usage fields reported zero, so token volume uses local o200k_base counts from the actual eval input text and final output text across five 24-row runs. This is an estimate before discounts, taxes, cache effects, tools, hosting, and provisioned-capacity charges.

spread.takeaway: The optimized assets remove the noisy baseline behavior.

optimizer.takeaway: The optimizer changed the instructions and the retrieval tool contract.

evals.takeaway: All three are hosted-agent evals with the same held-out dataset and rubric.

behavior.takeaway: RFT is a model swap after the optimizer fixed the behavior.

model.takeaway: The tuned run swaps the model from gpt-6-astra to the MAI RFT deployment.

rftJob.takeaway: The preserved, successful MAI RFT job.

deployment.takeaway: The serving comparison uses the tuned deployment.

costEvidence.takeaway: Uses published Global Standard token rates. The actual bill can differ by discount, cache, tools, hosting, or capacity model.

results.title: Final results
results.body: The fresh Foundry replay starts from a deliberately mediocre baseline, applies {{candidate}}, then swaps only the model deployment to the MAI RFT model. Optimized passed {{optimized}} rows. Tuned MAI also passed {{tuned}}.
